top_choice_rationale: P001 awards a single, mature and well-delimited achievement: the optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms realised at fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, independently reproduced and used for tests of fundamental constants and relativity. The two-name allocation to Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (record accuracy and stability) is defensible, and the citation can name the lattice mechanism to separate it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. The overlap with earlier precision-measurement prizes is a real reservation but does not outweigh the case, so an award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my background is in string theory and cosmology, not atomic physics
